page: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a bare-metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family powered by a single AMD EPYC 7443P processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 24 physical cores and 48 execution threads clocked at 2.85 GHz with dedicated allocation. The configuration includes 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, allocating 5.33 GB per core thread. The instance incorporates 960 GB of local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results show robust multi-threaded processing and strong system throughput across varied tests. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core performance alongside strong multi-core results, registering a score of 77,709.84. Geekbench testing reflects solid parallel capabilities, recording a multi-core score of 16,781, with clang software compilation and ray tracing tasks placing in the upper quartile. PassMark testing mirrors this behavior with an overall CPU score of 60,061.01, supported by top-tier memory scores and strong results in cryptographic encryption and database operations.

From an architectural standpoint, the dedicated physical hardware eliminates hypervisor contention, delivering consistent execution latency. However, tradeoffs include reliance on DDR4 memory channels rather than newer memory generations, producing moderate read and write memory bandwidth. The processor supports standard AVX and cryptographic acceleration such as AES and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. Additionally, local storage is limited to a single 960 GB SSD volume, which restricts local data capacity for storage-dense workloads.

This server architecture suits compute-heavy and memory-intensive production tasks that benefit from non-virtualized single-tenant infrastructure. Key deployment targets include relational database systems, multi-threaded software build pipelines, concurrent microservices environments, and intermediate batch processing tasks requiring high CPU core density paired with balanced memory allocation.
